connections.name: Alexandr Wang
connections.description: Zuckerberg recruited Wang in June 2025, when Meta bought 49% of Scale AI for about $14.3 billion; Wang leads Meta Superintelligence Labs, which reports directly to Zuckerberg.

sources.title: Mark Zuckerberg overhauled Meta's AI org around superintelligence and Alexandr Wang — Fortune

connections.name: Dustin Moskovitz
connections.description: Co-founded Facebook with Zuckerberg in their Harvard dorm in 2004.

connections.name: Marc Andreessen
connections.description: Andreessen has sat on the board of Zuckerberg's Facebook (now Meta) since June 2008; both were also named to PCAST in March 2026.

connections.name: Palmer Luckey
connections.description: Facebook bought Luckey's Oculus in 2014 and he worked there until March 2017, leaving amid controversy over his pro-Trump donation (Facebook says his politics were not the reason). In May 2025 Anduril and Meta announced a partnership on military XR headsets.

sources.title: Controversial Oculus founder Palmer Luckey leaves Facebook — SiliconANGLE

connections.name: Peter Thiel
connections.description: Thiel became Facebook's first outside investor in August 2004, buying 10.2% for $500,000, and sat on its board from 2005 to 2022.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: Weeks after Zuckerberg dined with Trump at Mar-a-Lago in November 2024, Meta gave $1 million to Trump's inaugural fund; neither he nor Meta had given to Trump's 2017 or Biden's 2021 funds.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
current_role: Co-founder, chairman, CEO and controlling shareholder of Meta Platforms
summary: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook at Harvard in 2004 with Dustin Moskovitz and others, took it public in 2012 and controls its parent Meta, now a leading AI spender (Meta Superintelligence Labs, led by Alexandr Wang). Once attacked by Trump, he dined with him at Mar-a-Lago after the 2024 election, and Meta gave $1 million to Trump's inaugural fund.

sources.title: Meta gave $1 million to Trump's inaugural fund — Axios
